feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/strategy depth. It reads professionally, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles with increasing responsibility and strategic scope.  
- Strong credibility through concrete platforms, tools, and scale indicators like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and analytics stack details.  
- Writing is polished and audience-appropriate, with a strong executive summary and consistent focus on digital strategy, governance, and mission-driven communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, email performance, engagement gains, efficiency improvements, cost savings, or team size managed.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs. later lists without final commas); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It reads clearly, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and fix grammar: use “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current senior value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Add one clearer differentiator from the experience section, such as enterprise web ecosystems, governance, or advocacy-focused digital transformation.
- Reduce broad channel lists to avoid sounding like a skills inventory.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that support complex communications operations. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- The channel list overlaps with multiple experience bullets; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be stronger if tightened around differentiating strengths and phrased more consistently.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications • CMS & web operations • Editorial workflow & governance • Analytics & performance reporting • Systems architecture & automation • Stakeholder coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production”
- Replace “multi-channel communication” with “cross-channel communications” for more natural phrasing and consistency with the header.
- Consider swapping in a more distinctive capability such as “CMS modernization” or “AI-enabled search strategy” to reflect recent consulting work.
- If space allows, group by strategic/technical/operational strengths rather than mixing broad and narrow items.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy,” “analytics,” “multimedia,” and “workflow/systems” are already covered in more detail in Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, ownership, and the most distinctive work so it complements—rather than repeats—your NACo leadership entries.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization in a full-time freelance engagement.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets and add measurable outcomes where possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search improvement metrics, workflow time saved.
- Emphasize distinctive recent work: Drupal campaign builds, enterprise content/workflow design, and AI-enabled search; e.g., “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo governance/operations bullets—make this more specific or outcome-based.
- Campaign microsites and AI search also appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and reserve project detail for that section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management themes already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and cross-channel communications strategy.”
- Combine scope + flagship achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused; add performance if available: email list size, engagement growth, social growth, video output, event reach, or cost/time savings from the studio.
- Tighten the analytics/governance bullets: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery” and “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video/programming language also appears in prior NACo entries; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more as support than leadership. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and concrete outputs that set up the promotion to Director.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show ownership and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership: “Built cross-team editorial planning and standardized digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/ownership, not creation alone.
- “Publishing workflows/governance” overlaps with the Director role; avoid repeating standards/governance language unless you add a distinct result.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for complex publishing teams
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy, content planning & UX
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want stronger alignment with recent roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale instead of broad terms here (e.g., “50+ publishers,” “10,000+ page web ecosystems”) rather than in this skills block.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths rather than listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, impact-oriented line: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older items here: cut jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent work.
- Consider dropping either SharePoint or Power Pages from this topline line unless they are important to target roles; keep the strongest/recent platforms first.
- If space allows, make the lead term more senior: replace “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” with “Enterprise Web Platforms & Technical Delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for the technical section.
- “CMS modernization” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Enterprise website modernization.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” This topline item should emphasize decision-making value and optimization outcomes, not just repeat platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy & KPI design
- Executive and leadership reporting
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity
- SEO, UX insight and performance optimization
- Put the business outcome first: “turning digital performance data into reporting and optimization decisions.”
- Consider replacing “SEO and performance analysis” with “SEO, user behavior analysis and conversion/performance optimization” for clearer impact.
- If space allows, align with recent experience by highlighting enterprise reporting infrastructure rather than generic analysis.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.
- Tool list also repeats almost exactly from “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep this section more strategic and less exhaustive.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent relevance rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations
- Virtual event and recurring advocacy content delivery
- Consider renaming to “Video, Livestream & Event Production” for clearer, more modern phrasing.
- Replace “video production and editing” with “broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to signal level, not just activity.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill area to scale/results from recent roles (e.g., built NACo’s first in-house studio; supported recurring advocacy programming).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are also reinforced in Work Experience, so keep this section concise and non-repetitive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s very generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add proficiency/context or be tightened to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by relevance/recency: Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider adding level/scope instead of just names, e.g., Drupal (10,000+ page migration), SharePoint (intranet/content ops), WordPress (campaign/editorial sites)
- If no context can be added, shorten to the 3–4 most relevant platforms rather than listing every CMS

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” Topline Skills entry almost exactly; consider removing one or merging them
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise focus elsewhere unless supported by a project example

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and tools that support recent, higher-impact work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If space allows, add light context instead of just tools: Front-end development (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations • Tag management (Google Tag Manager) • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • CI/CD and deployment workflows (GitHub Actions)
- Consider replacing older/basic terms like “HTML5”/“CSS3” with “Front-end development” to sound more senior and less checklist-driven.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you want this section focused strictly on implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a flat list to grouped systems: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first based on recent work: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira/Asana.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show application, e.g. “used for editorial planning, approvals, intake, and cross-team coordination.”
- Consider trimming one or two lower-value collaboration tools if they are not central; Slack/Teams can feel generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar signals—listing all four may look unfocused unless grouped.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since the CV already shows strong email leadership in recent NACo roles, this item should be tightened and framed around enterprise email/member engagement systems rather than repeating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations and member engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was light exposure, remove it to preserve credibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding outcome claims here unless they are not already stated elsewhere.
- “Engagement” also overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations,” so keep this item tool-focused, not strategic.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup role rather than showing concrete contributions. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and recurring multimedia outputs, with metrics if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and scope: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Make contributions more concrete: “Supported a major website refresh and improved cross-channel publishing workflows.”
- Clarify outputs and ownership: “Produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/videos, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early-building the format.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and a standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Condense the rest into one support statement: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and member engagement.”
- Add any measurable detail if available: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this higher-level and more innovation/program-focused.
- Avoid overemphasizing video or channel management here, since those are covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
